title: After 8 Months in Power, How Much Has the BNP Changed Bangladesh?
gist: Eight months into BNP rule under PM Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh shows mixed results: remittances up 13.1 percent and inflation eased but still around 8.3 percent, with stagnant growth, falling revenue, persistent mob violence, and reforms that critics say weaken independent oversight.

insights.claim: Police recorded 2,122 murder cases in March-September versus 2,317 a year earlier, with robbery and kidnapping down slightly, but burglary rose about 13 percent to 2,022 and total registered cases rose 14 percent to 125,763, mostly narcotics cases.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Headline crime improvement is marginal; the narcotics jump may reflect enforcement rather than prevalence.

insights.claim: Ain o Salish Kendra counted 131 people killed in mob beatings between March and August 2026, with police present but failing to stop several attacks.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Mob violence is a persistent governance and investor-confidence risk.

insights.claim: A Dhaka crime analyst argues that the police have still not been depoliticized, that influential drug patrons remain beyond the law, and that no significant improvement has occurred over the past one and a half years.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Institutional reform of policing remains the missing piece for security improvements.
insights.quote: The Bangladesh Police has still not been depoliticized

insights.claim: Inflation was 8.34 percent in September, barely below September 2025's 8.36 percent after peaking at 9.42 percent in May, while the lower-paid wage index rose only 8.05 percent in August, meaning real wages are still falling.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Household purchasing power remains squeezed, weighing on domestic demand.

insights.claim: Remittances reached $18.94 billion between March and August, up 13.1 percent year on year, helping replenish foreign exchange reserves.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Remittances are the main external support for reserves and the taka.

insights.claim: Businesses are cautious, with weak demand, expensive borrowing, energy shortages and idle factory capacity limiting investment, so the return of an elected government has not yet revived credit growth.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Weak private credit demand suggests no near-term capex recovery.

insights.claim: Diesel prices were raised from 115 to 135 taka per liter in September because Middle East conflict lifted energy costs, threatening transport and production costs and the recent easing of inflation.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve

insights.claim: Revenue for July-August was 518.9 billion taka versus 547.7 billion a year earlier and 291.6 billion below target, while the record 9.38 trillion taka budget assumes nearly 7 trillion taka in revenue.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Large fiscal gap raises the likelihood of borrowing, spending cuts or new taxes.

insights.claim: An industrial economist warns that Biman's orders for 25 Boeing and 10 Airbus aircraft against a current fleet of 19, plus public salary increases, could create long-term debt without management reforms, and that high inflation, weak growth and rising unemployment indicate stagnation.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: State-airline capex and salary rises compound fiscal stress.

insights.claim: Rahman has visited Malaysia, China and the UNGA but not India, because Sheikh Hasina remains in India and Dhaka seeks extradition; the Ganges water treaty expires in December, giving India talks urgency.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: The December treaty expiry is a near-term flashpoint in India-Bangladesh relations.

insights.claim: China backed cooperation on Mongla Port, the Chinese Economic and Industrial Zone in Chittagong and the Teesta project during Rahman's June visit, but no completed financing was announced and the Teesta water-sharing dispute with India remains separate.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Chinese infrastructure involvement is rising; watch for financing announcements.

insights.claim: The inherited US-Bangladesh tariff deal set a 19 percent US tariff with preferential garment treatment linked to US textile input purchases and locked in agricultural and energy purchase commitments; Biman ordered 11 more Boeing aircraft on September 23 partly to ease trade tensions.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Garment export tariffs are managed through purchase commitments; watch for further US tariff pressure.

insights.claim: Constitutional reforms endorsed in the February referendum, including a 10-year premiership limit, a second chamber and judicial safeguards, remain stalled, as BNP refused the Constitutional Reform Council route and the opposition boycotted the parliamentary committee, with discussions targeted for December.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Delay raises the risk that reforms are diluted to BNP preferences.

insights.claim: Laws passed September 6 on the National Human Rights Commission and enforced disappearances, and the replacement of the Rapid Action Battalion with the Special Response Battalion, were criticized by Human Rights Watch as weakening independent oversight of security forces.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Points to institutional backsliding risk and potential Western rights pressure.

insights.claim: The BNP kept the interim government's ban on Awami League activities, and Human Rights Watch reported at least 10 Awami League office holders died in prison since BNP took office, with hundreds held without charge.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Excluding a major party reduces the electoral legitimacy and stability of the political settlement.
insights.locator: Political Environment and Freedom of Expression

insights.claim: Draft cyber law amendments could jail journalists for up to 10 years over rumors or misinformation, and Ain o Salish Kendra logged 242 journalist harassment incidents March-September; the government agreed to form two committees on safeguards.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Media-freedom tightening is a governance risk to watch.
insights.locator: Political Environment and Freedom of Expression

insights.claim: A Dhaka University analyst expects the BNP to proceed according to its own preferences and priorities despite the referendum mandate, seeing the beginnings of institutional mechanisms that could weaken opposition and dissent.
insights.speaker: Saqlain Rizve
insights.so_what: Suggests consolidation of power rather than genuine institutional reform.
insights.quote: I think the BNP will ultimately proceed according to its own preferences and priorities
